issues.legal_issue: An appellate disciplinary body may remit a charge for reasoned reconsideration in an advocate’s appeal even when no separate appeal has been brought against the disposition of that charge.
material_facts: A state disciplinary committee found misconduct on two charges but its treatment of a third charge was read as an exoneration, without adequate reasons for its conclusion.
The advocate appealed, and the national disciplinary committee remitted the third charge to the state committee to give reasons.
The advocate challenged the remand on the ground that no aggrieved person had appealed the favorable disposition of the third charge.
The advocate had not given evidence before the state disciplinary committee, and the respondent stated that the remand had been made at the advocate’s counsel’s request.
issues.conclusion: The national disciplinary committee had jurisdiction to remit the charge for reasons, notwithstanding the absence of a separate appeal against the apparent exoneration. The Supreme Court dismissed the advocate’s appeal and left the remand in place.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 35 and 36 of the Advocates Act, 1961, disciplinary jurisdiction is exercised to address professional or other misconduct. Section 37(2) gives the Bar Council of India’s disciplinary committee broad appellate power to pass an order it deems fit, including varying punishment; that power may be exercised in an appeal brought by the advocate and is not confined by the technical rule against disturbing an acquittal. The power remains bounded by the statute and must be exercised in a manner germane to its purposes. The Court relied on O.N. Mahindroo v. District Judge for the breadth of disciplinary appellate powers and the inapplicability of autrefois acquit or convict, V.C. Ranjadurai v. D. Gopalan for the requirement that an order be germane to the Act and its purposes, Raja Ram Mahadev Paranjype v. Aba Maruti Mali for the limits on discretionary statutory powers, and Ade Pherozshah Gandhi v. H.M. Seervai for the legislative development of appellate rights and powers. It distinguished Makeshwar Nath Srivastava v. State of Bihar as inapplicable.

rule.if: disciplinary_appeal_from_state_committee and advocate_is_appellant and charge_disposition_lacks_adequate_reasons and remand_is_germane_to_professional_discipline

predicates.disciplinary_appeal_from_state_committee: The proceeding is an appeal from a state body’s decision in a professional disciplinary matter.
predicates.advocate_is_appellant: The advocate whose conduct is under review brought the appeal.
predicates.charge_disposition_lacks_adequate_reason: The state body disposed of a charge without giving adequate reasons for its conclusion.
predicates.remand_is_germane_to_professional_discip: The proposed remand is directed to resolving the disciplinary matter consistently with the purposes of professional discipline.

issues.definition: When an advocate appeals a state disciplinary decision, an inadequately reasoned disposition of a charge may be remitted for reconsideration if the remand serves the purposes of professional discipline.
